title: HiState: Hierarchical Prefix Cache Management for Hybrid LLM Serving in Agentic Workloads
summary: HiState replaces the prefix-cache policies in hybrid-model serving stacks such as vLLM-Marconi and SGLang-HiCache, which retain recurrent checkpoints only at selected boundaries and therefore miss or recompute reusable prefixes in agent workloads. It adds SSD-tiered checkpoint storage, adaptive checkpoint-interval control, and unified eviction, which increases storage-management complexity and requires SSD capacity; the recurrent-checkpoint read is bounded per hit, but the KV path still depends on fast memory. It can fail when the serving stack or model is not a supported hybrid architecture, when SSD latency or capacity is misconfigured, or when the workload lacks the agentic prefix-reuse patterns that justify the extra hierarchy.
rationale: The gains are specific to hybrid models and agent-trace reuse patterns, so a constrained team should track the technique but only trial it if they already serve hybrid models with similar workloads.
technique: Hierarchical prefix cache management for hybrid LLM agent serving
